title: MATH GAOKAO - 147
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Use a reduction formula to simplify \(\sin(180^\circ-\theta)\).
questions.question:
Assume \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\). Simplify
\[
\sin(180^\circ-\theta).
\]
questions.explanation:
The angle \(180^\circ-\theta\) lies in quadrant II for an acute angle \(\theta\). In quadrant II, sine is positive, and the reference angle is \(\theta\). Therefore,
\[
\sin(180^\circ-\theta)=\sin\theta.
\]
questions.hint: Determine the quadrant of the angle and use the reference angle.

questions.learningObjective: Use a reduction formula to simplify \(\cos(180^\circ-\theta)\).
questions.question:
Assume \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\). Simplify
\[
\cos(180^\circ-\theta).
\]
questions.explanation:
The angle \(180^\circ-\theta\) lies in quadrant II. In quadrant II, cosine is negative, and the reference angle is \(\theta\). Therefore,
\[
\cos(180^\circ-\theta)=-\cos\theta.
\]
questions.hint: Determine the sign of cosine in quadrant II and use the reference angle.

questions.learningObjective: Use a cofunction reduction formula to simplify \(\sin(90^\circ+\theta)\).
questions.question:
Assume \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\). Simplify
\[
\sin(90^\circ+\theta).
\]
questions.explanation:
Using the cofunction identity,
\[
\sin(90^\circ+\theta)=\cos\theta.
\]
Equivalently, the angle \(90^\circ+\theta\) lies in quadrant II, where sine is positive, and its reference angle is \(90^\circ-\theta\). Thus the result is \(\cos\theta\).
questions.hint: Use the cofunction relationship between sine and cosine.

questions.learningObjective: Use a cofunction reduction formula to simplify \(\cos(90^\circ+\theta)\).

Assume \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\). Simplify
\[
\cos(90^\circ+\theta).
\]
questions.explanation:
Using the cofunction identity,
\[
\cos(90^\circ+\theta)=-\sin\theta.
\]
Equivalently, the angle \(90^\circ+\theta\) lies in quadrant II, where cosine is negative, and its reference angle is \(90^\circ-\theta\). Thus the result is \(-\sin\theta\).
questions.hint: Use the cofunction relationship and the sign of cosine in quadrant II.

questions.learningObjective: Use a reduction formula to simplify \(\tan(180^\circ-\theta)\).
questions.question:
Simplify
\[
\tan(180^\circ-\theta).
\]
questions.explanation:
Using the identity for tangent,
\[
\tan(180^\circ-\theta)=\frac{\sin(180^\circ-\theta)}{\cos(180^\circ-\theta)}.
\]
From reduction formulas,
\[
\sin(180^\circ-\theta)=\sin\theta,\qquad \cos(180^\circ-\theta)=-\cos\theta.
\]
Thus
\[
\tan(180^\circ-\theta)=\frac{\sin\theta}{-\cos\theta}=-\tan\theta.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tan(180^\circ-\theta)=-\tan\theta.
\]
questions.hint: Express tangent in terms of sine and cosine, then apply the reduction formulas.

Using the identity for tangent,
\[
\tan(90^\circ+\theta)=\frac{\sin(90^\circ+\theta)}{\cos(90^\circ+\theta)}.
\]
From cofunction reduction formulas,
\[
\sin(90^\circ+\theta)=\cos\theta,\qquad \cos(90^\circ+\theta)=-\sin\theta.
\]
Thus
\[
\tan(90^\circ+\theta)=\frac{\cos\theta}{-\sin\theta}=-\cot\theta.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tan(90^\circ+\theta)=-\cot\theta.
\]
questions.hint: Express tangent in terms of sine and cosine, then apply the cofunction reduction formulas.
